newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds continue firm tone, quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds continue firm tone, quiet trade.

text.p: Argentine bonds were on a stable footing late morning Tuesday as the market kept last week's positive tone, albeit amid quiet activity.
"There is no euphoria but the market is well underpinned," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/8 at 94-1/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.25 at 124.20.
Another trader said Latin American markets in general were supported by talk that Ecuador may be considering a debt buyback.
Otherwise, with Argentine bonds having soared to record highs last week, traders said this week's activity was set to consolidate those gains.

U.S. monetary policy continued to be a prime focus ahead of July's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee. U.S. retail sales and producer price figures due for release later in the week were seen giving more clues to whether the Federal Reserve will hike rates again in July.
